title: iOS 27: What’s new, the latest problems, and what’s coming next
content:
Macworld





Apple unveiled iOS 27 at WWDC on June 8, 2026, with the public release following on September 14. The latest update, iOS 27.2.1 arrived on November 9, with security fixes. It follows the October 26 release of iOS 27.2, which introduced further Siri AI improvements and new app features. 
iOS 27 mainly focuses on three key areas: Siri AI, a rebuilt assistant with its own dedicated app; new child safety and parental controls; and system improvements designed to make everyday tasks faster and easier. iOS 27 supports the iPhone 11 and later, plus the iPhone SE (2nd generation) and later, although some Apple Intelligence and Siri features require newer hardware.
This guide covers iOS 27’s biggest features, compatible iPhones and what’s coming in future updates. We regularly update it with the latest public release and beta developments, newly discovered features and reported problems.
Updated November 27: Following the release of iOS 27.2 and 27.2.1, some iPhone users have reported problems including apps crashing, freezing, or failing to load content, raising concerns about potential memory-management and network connectivity issues.


What’s New in iOS 27 at a Glance
Siri AI: Apple’s new Siri AI combines personal context, onscreen awareness and web knowledge to deliver more natural conversations, richer answers, app actions and cross-device chat history.
Apple Intelligence across apps: Apple Intelligence expands across Safari, Photos, Messages, Mail, Calendar, Home and Shortcuts, adding smarter suggestions, automation, image generation and context-aware assistance.
Smarter Photos editing: Photos gains Spatial Reframing, Extend and an upgraded Clean Up tool, allowing users to improve composition, expand images and remove distractions more naturally.
Child safety and parental controls: New parental controls include Ask to Browse, Time Allowances, app schedules and enhanced Communication Safety tools. Activating the redesigned experience through Family Sharing requires every eligible family device to be running version 27 or later.
System Improvements: Apple has made many system operations faster and more efficient, which will be especially noticeable on older phones. Battery life may be longer, and there are dozens of small quality-of-life improvements throughout the system and its apps.
iPhone Handoff: iPhone Handoff in iOS 27 lets two eSIM-equipped iPhones share one number, switching calls, messages and Find My location when unlocked. It requires matching Apple Accounts and carrier support. T-Mobile offers it; Verizon and EE plan support. Fees may apply. More information below.






What’s coming in the next iOS 27 update – and when?
Next iOS update: iOS 27.3 – expected in December 2026.
Latest developer beta: iOS 27.3 beta 2, released November 16, 2026. Revised developer beta 2 build, 24C5049f, released November 19
Latest public beta: iOS 27.3 public beta 2, released November 19, 2026.
Apple is currently beta testing iOS 27.3, which we expect to be released in December 2026. The update is set to bring further Siri AI improvements, a redesigned Health app, new Safari features, and additional functionality for iPhone Duo owners.
The following new features and improvements have been discovered in the iOS 27.3 betas and are expected to be available when the update is released to the public:
Expanded Siri actions: Siri gains more capabilities within Apple’s apps, while developers can begin testing new integrations for third-party apps.
More Siri AI languages: Traditional Chinese, Norwegian, Turkish and Vietnamese are being tested.
Apple Intelligence in China: Initial features include Writing Tools, Visual Intelligence, Clean Up and Genmoji. Siri AI remains unavailable.
Redesigned Health app: The new design returns after appearing briefly during iOS 27.2 testing.
Siri access to Health data: Reports indicate that Siri AI can answer questions about information stored in the Health app in the iOS 27.3 beta. Privacy details still need confirmation, as Apple’s current support documentation says Health data cannot be read by Siri AI.
Safari’s Ask about Page: On supported devices, Siri can answer questions using an entire webpage, including content outside the visible screen, and use the results in follow-up tasks.
Safari Adaptive Dark Mode: An optional setting adapts bright webpages for dark mode. Users can exclude individual websites.
Safari vertical tabs: The beta adds a vertical tab layout on iPhone Duo, displaying tabs down the side of the screen.
iPhone Duo front-camera unlocking: An optional setting lets users unlock the closed phone with its front camera after recent Touch ID or passcode authentication. Touch ID is still required for Apple Pay and passwords, and after approximately 45 minutes of inactivity.
iPhone Duo Close to Lock: A new option under Settings > Display & Brightness lets users lock the phone by closing it.
iPhone Duo Reachability: Content can shift sideways to make the wider display easier to reach.
StandBy customization: The beta brings more color and layout options to StandBy on regular iPhones. StandBy still requires the phone to be charging. Users can touch and hold the StandBy screen to add, edit or delete a custom layout.
Apple Watch Audio Intelligence: Live Rewind and Siri Recap are available for testing with an Apple Watch Series 12 or Ultra 4.
Fitness+ Gym Strength: In the 27.3 betas, Fitness+ can build strength-training plans around your equipment, schedule and readiness, with adjustable weights and repetitions. It requires a Fitness+ subscription, watchOS 27.3 beta and an iPhone or iPad running the corresponding 27.3 beta.
Apple Music Selfie Sing: The beta lets Apple Music subscribers record short selfie videos with song details and synchronized lyrics. The Selfie Sing button appears in the lyrics view for compatible songs, although the supported selection is currently limited.
Video podcasts in Apple TV: Video episodes from Apple Podcasts are being added to the Apple TV app, with playback progress synced between the two apps.
More News+ puzzles: New puzzles are available for subscribers in the U.K., Australia and French Canada, with availability varying by region.
iCloud public-link checks: Apple says that starting with iOS 27.3, it will check photos, files and other iCloud content shared using “Anyone with the link” for harmful content. These items are accessible to Apple and aren’t end-to-end encrypted, even if Advanced Data Protection is enabled. The checks apply to items shared through this public-link option, rather than everything stored in iCloud. To restrict access to invited recipients, choose “People you choose” when sharing.






iOS 27 latest version: What’s in iOS 27.2.1
Apple released iOS 27.2.1 on November 9, 2026, addressing several security vulnerabilities affecting Messages, Bluetooth, AirPlay and other system components.
Two particularly concerning flaws in Messages could allow a remote attacker to join an iMessage group conversation and receive its messages, or enable someone added to a group to access messages sent before they joined. Apple has fixed both issues.
The update also addresses Bluetooth vulnerabilities that could allow a malicious nearby device to pair without user interaction, as well as weaknesses that could allow attackers to bypass limits on AirPlay pairing-code attempts. Another fix prevents apps from potentially accessing sensitive user information without proper authorization.
Should you install iOS 27.2.1?
Apple has not confirmed that these vulnerabilities have been actively exploited, but we would normally encourage users to install the update to protect their devices. However, given a number of issues with iOS 27.2 and iOS 27.2.1 described below, we would recommend waiting. 
To update an iPhone, go to Settings > General > Software Update.






Problems with iOS 27.2 and iOS 27.2.1

				
					

				
			
It just won’t load. 

Foundry




We’re tracking bugs and other issues reported by iPhone users following the release of iOS 27 and subsequent updates, including problems we’ve encountered ourselves at Macworld, along with potential fixes and workarounds.
Apps crashing or failing to load 
Following the release of iOS 27.2 and iOS 27.2.1, some iPhone users have reported apps freezing, crashing unexpectedly or failing to load content despite an active Wi-Fi or cellular connection. Reports on Reddit and the MacRumors forums suggest that both Apple and third-party apps are affected, including Safari, Facebook and Instagram.
Apps failing to load content: Macworld staff have experienced problems with both the Amazon and Facebook apps on an iPhone 17 since updating to iOS 27.2.1. In both apps, images frequently fail to load, while comments in Facebook also fail to appear. There have also been instances of webpages failing to load in Safari. The symptoms could point to a memory-management or network connectivity issue.
Apple Music storage issue: Macworld has also encountered an unusual storage issue on an iPhone 17, where music that had been downloaded without the user’s knowledge was taking up a significant amount of storage space. It emerged that the Music app was automatically adding favorited songs to the library. To prevent this, go to Settings > Apps > Music and turn off the option to automatically add favorite songs. You may also want to disable Automatic Downloads to prevent songs added to your library from being downloaded to your iPhone.

				
					

				
			Stop Apple Music FROM downloading EVERYTHING!

Foundry




While these problems may be unrelated, reports from other iPhone users experiencing app stability and connectivity issues suggest that there could be an underlying iOS bug. It is unclear whether memory or storage management is a contributing factor.
Restarting the iPhone or force-quitting affected apps appears to temporarily resolve the issues for some users. Apple has not publicly acknowledged the problems, and it remains unclear whether they stem from a wider iOS bug or individual app compatibility issues.






iOS 27 version history: Every update and release date
What did iOS 27.0.1 add? The first update was iOS 27.0.1, released on September 28. It fixed unexpected restarts following failed Face ID authentication, a 2x-camera color artifact affecting iPhone 18 Pro models, and an iOS 27 touchscreen freeze triggered by opening Notification Center and Control Center simultaneously. iOS 27.0.1 also has a preventive role in a cellular problem that Apple did not mention in its published release notes. Apple confirmed that a small number of iPhone 18 Pro Max models on AT&T can lose cellular service, preventing calls, texts and data access and potentially affecting 911 calls. Some owners reported their phones dropping into SOS mode despite previously showing a strong 5G signal.
What did iOS 27.1 add? Apple released iOS 27.1 on October 23, 2026, exclusively for the iPhone Duo; other iPhone models moved directly from iOS 27.0.1 to iOS 27.2.
What did iOS 27.2 add? Apple released iOS 27.2 on October 26, 2026. It improves Siri AI’s memory and personal context, expands language support, and adds Suggestions in Messages alongside other app improvements, bug fixes and security updates. Dual Capture arrives for Group FaceTime calls, while iPhone Duo gains Apple Pencil (USB-C) support and Edge Light to illuminate your face during video calls. Shared Albums in Photos gains editable captions and comments, helps avoid duplicate photos, and provides reminders to save photos and videos before temporary albums expire. Read our iOS 27.2 guide for more details.






What features are still to come in iOS 27
At the time of the launch of iOS 27 not all of Apple’s promised features were available. Several were added in iOS 27.2, but there are still a couple that we’re waiting on.
Redesigned Health app: Having been removed in earlier beta testing, the new Health app design has returned in the iOS 27.3 beta.
Automatic password changes: The ability for the Passwords app to visit supported websites and automatically replace compromised passwords was removed shortly before release. 






What does Siri AI do in iOS 27

				
					

				
			
Apple




By far the biggest upgrade in iOS 27 is Siri AI – an entirely new architecture for Siri. Apple says it is more personal, conversational, and capable than the current assistant, with support for natural follow-up questions, personal context, onscreen awareness and up-to-date information from the web.
Siri AI features
The next wave of Siri AI features is currently in beta testing and is expected to become available with iOS 27.3 in December 2026, although wider integration with third-party apps is not expected until spring 2027.
More natural conversations: Siri AI is able to understand open-ended questions, follow-up requests and more complex natural language, making interactions feel less like issuing simple voice commands.
Personal context: Siri can draw on information stored in Messages, Mail, Photos and Notes to find details and answer questions. For example, you could ask it to find information buried in an old email or message.
Onscreen awareness: Siri can understand what you’re viewing and act on it, such as saving an address from a message, adding an event to Calendar or answering questions about an article.
Camera intelligence: A new Siri Camera mode lets you show Siri something through the iPhone’s camera, then ask questions or perform actions based on what it sees.
More capable app actions: Siri can perform tasks within apps such as Messages, Music and Reminders. It can, for example, edit a recently sent message, add a song to a playlist or handle more complex Apple Music requests. (Partially available now: Editing recently sent messages, creating and saving playlists, and several other advanced app actions are coming in iOS 27.3.)
Better general knowledge and web answers: Siri can use information from the web to answer questions about recent events and tackle more specific or complicated queries than before.
Conversation history across devices: A dedicated Siri app lets users revisit previous conversations, pin important chats and continue conversations across Apple devices using iCloud syncing.
More natural Siri voices: Siri gains more expressive voices, with controls on compatible devices for adjusting speaking pace and expressiveness. Voice customization requires an iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone Air or newer.
Improved dictation: Better speech recognition, automatic punctuation, capitalization and formatting allow users to dictate more naturally when converting speech into text.
AI-assisted message replies: Siri can compose contextual replies in Messages using the conversation, personal information and web searches. Shortcuts can also automate replies to selected contacts, although manual Siri-assisted replies allow users to check and edit the response before it is sent. (Partially available now).
iOS 27.2 added several further Siri AI improvements:
Recall information from previous conversations.
Use Messages photo attachments, Calendar attendees and voicemails, with better results from Safari history and Reading List.
Control app access for Siri, Search and suggestions through Excluded Apps.
Select and copy individual portions of Siri’s responses.
iOS 27.3 expands Siri’s actions across Apple apps, including Calendar, Messages, Music and Reminders. You can ask Siri what it can do within an app.
Third-party apps integration: Apple has opened a developer preview that lets third-party apps connect their content and actions to Siri AI. This requires developers to build support into their apps. Apple says App Store submissions using these capabilities will open in spring, so installing iOS 27.3 alone will not enable the new integrations across existing apps. Third-party app integration is not expected until spring 2027, when Apple plans to begin accepting App Store submissions that take advantage of the new capabilities.
If you haven’t got Siri AI yet find out how here: Why don’t I have Siri AI on my iPhone?
Read about what happened when we made Siri AI Answer all our Messages.
How good is Siri AI?
Siri AI represents a significant improvement over the old Siri, particularly when handling conversational questions, current information, and personal context. It also has a dedicated app where you can see and continue previous conversations, upload images or documents, and more.
Even in our early tests during the beta, Siri AI proved to be much more helpful and useful. 
It’s definitely one of the biggest reasons to upgrade to iOS 27, potentially changing Siri from a basic voice-command system into a more general way of interacting with the iPhone.
Apple’s approach to AI safety also appears more restrained than some rival chatbots, with Siri designed to avoid excessive flattery, pretending to be human, or responding inappropriately to potentially harmful requests.
Siri AI remains a beta feature. iOS 27.2 added French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish alongside English. Siri AI remains unavailable on iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch in the EU and mainland China. The EU restriction does not apply to Siri AI on Mac so Siri AI can be used on the Mac in the EU.
Regional Siri AI availability
Siri AI will not initially be available on iPhone or iPad in the EU. It will also remain unavailable in China while Apple works through regulatory issues. 
The first release only supported the English language, and initially had only Expressive Voices for English (UK) and English (US). Support for French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish arrived with iOS 27.2. 
Traditional Chinese, Norwegian, Turkish and Vietnamese support is being tested in the iOS 27.3 beta. Siri AI is still not available in mainland China.
Lack of Siri language support is separate to Apple Intelligence language support. 
Siri AI compatibility
Siri AI requires iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max, and all iPhone 16 models and later, and the “new expressive voices” feature requires an iPhone 17 Pro, 17 Pro Max, iPhone Air, iPhone 18 Pro or 18 Pro Max and currently supports US and UK English voices.
Siri AI age restriction: Siri AI is unavailable to children under 13.






Apple Intelligence across apps
As well as Siri AI, the enhanced Apple Intelligence will power new features in Apple’s core apps throughout iOS 27. Safari can organize tabs into topics, monitor webpages for changes and even build extensions from natural-language descriptions. Photos gains a new Spatial Reframing editing tools including an upgraded Clean Up feature. Messages, Mail, and Calendar can now understand context, suggest actions and create events from simple descriptions.
Usage limits: Some cloud-based Apple Intelligence features have daily allowances, including advanced Siri AI requests, intelligent photo editing, Image Playground and cloud models in Shortcuts. Within the iOS 27.3 beta, Apple has detailed higher allowances through eligible iCloud+ plans:
50GB: Standard device limit
200GB: Up to 2× the standard device limit
2TB: Up to 5× the standard device limit
6TB: Up to 10× the standard device limit
12TB: Up to 20× the standard device limit
Apple has not disclosed the number of requests included in the standard allowance. Each device has its own standard limits; additional iCloud+ capacity is shared across devices and participating family members. Basic Siri requests remain available after the advanced-request allowance is exhausted.
Regional restrictions apply: Apple says increased access through iCloud+ is unavailable in the U.K., EU, Brazil and South Korea, with increased Apple Intelligence access also unavailable in China.
In testing the 27.3 beta software, Macworld’s Mahmoud Itani encountered Siri AI’s daily usage limit after roughly 20 minutes of making requests on Apple TV, despite having a 2TB iCloud+ subscription. His iPad and Mac subsequently displayed warnings that they were approaching their limits. 






New features coming to apps in iOS 27
iOS 27 brings a mix of major Apple Intelligence upgrades and smaller quality-of-life improvements across Safari, Photos, Messages, AirPods, Passwords, Wallet, and other core iPhone apps. Apple is also making iOS more adaptable to different screen sizes and orientations, which are changes necessary for the iPhone Duo.
Safari
Safari can automatically group open tabs into topics, making related pages easier to find. A new Notify Me feature will monitor webpages and alert you to changes such as price drops or products coming back into stock.
There’s also a new Describe an Extension feature which lets users create custom Safari extensions simply by explaining what they want the extension to do.
In the iOS 27.3 beta, Safari gains Ask about Page on supported devices. This lets Siri draw on the entire webpage, including sections you haven’t scrolled to. For example, you can ask Siri to extract a packing list from a travel guide, then save it in Notes.

				
					

				
			

Apple




Photos
Photos gains significantly more powerful AI editing tools.
Reframe can alter the composition and perspective of an existing photo, while Extend generates new image content beyond the original frame when straightening a horizon or changing the aspect ratio.

				
					

				
			
Apple




Clean Up has also been improved, with Fast and High Quality modes for removing unwanted objects or details. High Quality mode can produce considerably more natural results, although more ambitious edits can still introduce distortions or invented details.
Photos also adds new categories and the ability to save a frame from a video as a full-resolution photo. The resulting HEIF or JPG retains the video’s original resolution, date, and location metadata rather than simply creating a screenshot.
Camera
iOS 27 features a new more customizable camera interface that lets you pin the controls you use most often. For the iPhone 18 Pro, there are also “pro controls” like white balance, shutter speed, and manual focus along with Apple Reference Image, an authentication system designed to prove that a photo or video was genuinely captured on an iPhone and has not subsequently been manipulated.
The new Siri mode in the Camera app is a more convenient and logical way to access the Visual Intelligence features that used to require either a long-press of the camera button or a Control Center button.
Messages

				
					

				
			
Foundry




Messages gets several useful improvements.
You can decide what the microphone button beside the text field does. Under Settings > Apps > Messages > Show in Text Field, it can be set to Record Audio, Start Dictation, or None. Disabling it does not remove either feature: dictation remains available from the keyboard and audio messages remain in the + menu.
Voice-message playback controls are easier to access. 
iOS 27.2 adds Suggestions in Messages, which uses the context of your conversations to suggest actions in apps such as Calendar and Reminders. For example, when you discuss dinner plans, Messages can suggest creating a Calendar invitation.
Messages in iOS 27 will gain smarter suggested replies that can better reflect the user’s writing style. (This was removed from the iOS 27 beta and wasn’t available at the launch of iOS 27).
Drawing

				
					

				
			
Foundry




A new dedicated Drawing app replaces the old hidden handwriting interface. Accessible from the + menu, it uses the familiar pens, colours and drawing controls found in Notes and Markup, with finished drawings sent as images.
Mail
Mail gains more context-aware smart replies, including responses that can better match the user’s usual writing style.
Apple Intelligence can also surface information from Mail elsewhere in iOS. For example, the Phone app could retrieve a flight confirmation number from an email when you call an airline.
Phone
A new Call Context feature can surface information that may be useful when on a call. Apple says the information is selected according to who you are calling rather than by listening to the conversation. For example, calling an airline could cause iOS to surface the relevant flight confirmation from Mail.
Birthday reminders can also appear when calling contacts whose birthdays are stored on the iPhone.
iPhone Handoff
iPhone Handoff in iOS 27 lets you switch between two iPhones while keeping the same phone number. The number is active on only one iPhone at a time. When you unlock one of the two iPhones, your calls, voicemail, messages—including SMS and RCS—and your Find My location will be linked to that iPhone. 
The feature will work on any iPhone running iOS 27, as long as it has an eSIM. Both phones must use the same Apple Account, with Messages in iCloud enabled and matching FaceTime/iMessage sign-ins. 
You will need a carrier and eligible plan that specifically support iPhone Handoff – an ordinary eSIM plan alone isn’t enough. iPhone Handoff is currently supported by T-Mobile in the U.S. ($5 a month), Deutsche Telekom in Germany (€6.95 a month or included with select plans), and, since October 26, EE in the U.K. (£5 a month or included with its Full Works Plus plan). Verizon has confirmed that it will support the feature for $10 a month but has yet to announce a launch date. AT&T has indicated that it has no immediate plans to support iPhone Handoff, while no other U.K. networks have announced support.
FaceTime
Dual Capture arrived in iOS 27.2, allowing Group FaceTime participants to share front- and rear-camera views simultaneously. 
iOS 27.2 also adds support for bringing a third-party sign language interpreter or live captioner into a FaceTime call, providing additional communication support for participants.
Passwords

				
					

				
			
Passwords in iOS 27 will fix things for you.

Apple




The Passwords app continues to warn about weak, reused and compromised credentials, but iOS 27 will go a step further – eventually. Automatic password changes are coming to the Passwords app in a future software update. Apple has not confirmed a release date.
The forthcoming feature will, with your permission, visit supported websites, change vulnerable passwords and save the replacement credentials automatically. See: Apple got rid of my biggest password headache.
The usefulness of the feature will depend on how widely websites are supported and how well it handles obstacles such as two-factor authentication and unusual account-management interfaces. 
Apple removed this ability to detect compromised passwords and replace them from the beta shortly before the release of iOS 27. It’s expected to arrive with a later update.
Shortcuts
Shortcuts gains Describe a Shortcut, allowing users to create automations simply by explaining what they want to happen.
Apple Intelligence interprets the request and assembles the appropriate actions across supported apps, potentially making Shortcuts significantly easier to use for people unfamiliar with building automations manually.
Calendar
Calendar can create or modify events from natural-language instructions.
Apple says the app can recognize contacts, locations, dates and other event details as users type, reducing the amount of information that needs to be entered manually.
Siri can also create complete Calendar entries for information that is on your screen in that moment, or by taking a picture with the Siri mode in the Camera app.
Image Playground
Image Playground is considerably more powerful and realistic.
Apple says it can create photorealistic images and lets users modify generated pictures simply by describing the changes they want. Individual objects can also be selected, resized, or repositioned.
iOS 27.2 adds SynthID support to help identify images generated or modified using Photos and Image Playground.
Wallet
Wallet can create custom passes from QR codes.
Users can add their own fields and information to the pass, and passes automatically sync to Apple Watch.
Weather
Weather gets a clearer, more detailed forecast interface, with rearranged information tiles and new 10-day views showing precipitation probability/amount and wind speed throughout each day.
Home app
Apple Intelligence comes to the Home app for compatible HomeKit Secure Video cameras. It can group related camera notifications, describe recorded video and highlight clips that appear particularly noteworthy.
Maps
Apple Maps improves Flyover using higher-quality aerial imagery and Visual Intelligence models.
Apple says this produces sharper architectural detail and more realistic rendering of elements such as individual trees.
Apple News+ 
In the iOS 27.3 beta, Apple News+ subscribers in the U.K. gain a daily quick crossword, crossword mini and Sudoku. Australian subscribers gain those puzzles plus Quartiles and Emoji Game, while French-Canadian subscribers gain Quartiles and Emoji Game.
Podcasts
Video podcasts become easier to use, with improved controls for switching between watching a podcast and simply listening to it.
iOS 27.2 also reorganizes the Podcasts app’s Home tab into two separate sections: New Episodes, where you can find the latest releases from shows you follow, and Continue Playing, where you can resume episodes you’ve already started. This makes it easier to distinguish new listening from unfinished episodes.
Fitness
Workout summaries have been redesigned to make them easier to share.
Users can also hide completed Fitness+ workouts.
Games 
iOS 27.2 improves the Games app’s Friends tab with more information about suggested friends. Friends’ player pages also show the games they’ve played recently, making it easier to find something to play together.
Apple TV 
iOS 27.2 adds Simple Profiles to the Apple TV app, allowing members of your household to have their own profiles with recommendations tailored to their viewing preferences.
The iOS 27.3 beta also adds video podcast episodes from Apple Podcasts to the Apple TV app, giving viewers another place to discover and watch them.






iOS 27 changes beyond the iPhone 
CarPlay
CarPlay gains an audio scrubber, giving drivers and passengers more direct control when moving through audio tracks and other content.
AirPods
iOS 27 introduces several new AirPods features.
A new Custom EQ lets users independently adjust bass, mids and treble using a simple three-band equalizer under Settings > AirPods > Audio and Routing > Equalizer > Custom.
Compatible AirPods also gain improved Precision Finding through Find My, making individual earbuds easier to locate.
Some features require both iOS 27 and compatible AirPods firmware.
Read How to tune your AirPods with a custom EQ in iOS 27.






Other changes in iOS 27
It’s not only individual apps that are seeing changes.
Home Screen and landscape mode
Apple is making iOS significantly more flexible when dealing with different screen orientations and sizes.
More Apple apps now work properly in landscape, including Health, Home, Music, Weather, and Watch. Dynamic Island and Live Activities can also adapt to landscape orientation. The Home Screen supports extra-large widgets.
These changes could simply improve iPhone usability, but they’re also well suited to Apple’s folding iPhone Duo.
iPhone Mirroring in macOS 27 has similarly become freely resizable, with Apple apps dynamically rearranging their interfaces as the window changes shape.
Liquid Glass refinements

				
					

				
			
Apple




Apple says Liquid Glass has been refined for better readability, more uniform refraction and improved contrast. A new slider lets users adjust the look from ultraclear to fully tinted, while updated icons, toolbars, sidebars and window shapes add polish.
Ringtones, alarms and alert volume
iOS 27 finally separates several sound-volume controls.
Instead of one combined Ringtone and Alerts slider, users can independently adjust:
Ringtones
Alarms and timers
Alerts and system sounds
The change is optional. Under Settings > Sounds & Haptics, turning off Match Ringtone Volume reveals separate controls.
Media and call volume continue to work independently as before.
Keyboard
iOS 27 introduces a new quick-paste control above the keyboard.
It lets you paste recently copied text, images or screenshots without having to long-press inside a text field, making everyday copy-and-paste considerably faster.
Apple has also made the Liquid Glass keyboard design more consistent across apps.
Privacy and Find My
iOS 27 introduces the ability to temporarily pause Find My location sharing without notifying the person with whom the location is normally shared.
Recovery and troubleshooting
Apple is also expanding the iPhone’s recovery interface, giving users more options for diagnosing problems and recovering an iPhone without immediately connecting it to another device.






System changes and how iOS 27 makes your iPhone faster
Alongside the headline AI features, Apple says iOS 27 includes a wide range of under-the-hood improvements designed to make iPhones faster, smoother and more efficient.
Apps can launch up to 30% faster, newly taken photos can appear in the Photos library up to 70% faster, and AirDrop transfers can be up to 80% quicker. External drive transfers should also improve, while updates to network performance and the system-wide search index are designed to make connectivity and finding information faster.
The company has also reworked core technologies including CPU scheduling, display performance and processing efficiency. These changes should benefit older iPhones in particular, with Apple promising smoother performance and more efficient battery use on devices as old as the iPhone 11 and second-generation iPhone SE.
Our testing of the iOS 27 beta supports those claims. On an iPhone 11 Pro Max, Camera launch time fell from 0.98 seconds in iOS 26 to 0.65 seconds in iOS 27, while Maps improved from 3.01 seconds to 1.36 seconds.
Everyday use also feels smoother, with more fluid animations, unlocking, Control Center and app transitions. The phone ran cooler during testing too, which could point to improved system efficiency and potentially better battery performance.
More broadly, iOS 27 appears focused on refinement rather than simply adding new features. Apple says it has addressed dozens of common user frustrations, while changes such as more adjustable Liquid Glass effects are intended to improve readability and general usability.
That focus should make iOS 27 particularly worthwhile for owners of older iPhones, even on models that do not support Siri AI. Those devices still gain performance improvements alongside features such as clipboard tools for the keyboard, independent alarm and timer volume controls, custom Wallet passes, Photos changes, larger widgets, and Liquid Glass refinements.






Child safety and parental controls

				
					

				
			
Apple




There are lots of improvements to parental controls, including new time allowances for entertainment, games, and social media, and new schedule tools for different times of day or days of the week.
This includes new features like an expansion of the existing “ask to buy” feature for apps to websites. Before a child can view a new website, they’ll have to ask for permission.
Ask to Browse: Will expand the current Ask to Buy feature to the web. Children will need to request permission before visiting new websites, and parents can review requests in Messages before approving.
Communication Safety: Communication Safety continues to help protect children from viewing or sharing nudity in Messages, FaceTime and other apps. Apple says it will also intervene before children see gore or violent content in shared images and videos.
Time Allowances and schedules: Parents can set Time Allowances across categories such as Entertainment, Games and Social Media. Recommendations are based on a child’s age combined with guidance from clinical and child development experts. Schedules let parents choose which apps are available at different times or on different days.
Redesigned Screen Time: Screen Time gets a redesigned interface with an at-a-glance view of average device usage and most-used apps. Apple says parents can quickly limit or extend access in the moment.
Child accounts and family safety: Apple says child accounts remain central to age-appropriate protections. Parents can manage app access, web access, communication permissions and Screen Time settings. 
Problems with Parental Control setup
Updating the parent’s iPhone is not enough to activate the redesigned Screen Time experience. Apple says every eligible iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch and Vision Pro in the Family Sharing group must be running the appropriate version 27 software.
Devices that cannot run version 27 are listed as Legacy Devices and can continue using the older Screen Time and Family Sharing system. Apple says these incompatible devices should not prevent supported devices from adopting the new controls.
To find out which devices need to be updated go to Settings > Family > View Family Devices. Once eligible devices are running iOS 27, go to Settings > Family > Get Started to transfer the family’s existing parental controls or set up new ones.
Some families have encountered delays, outdated device listings and eligible hardware incorrectly appearing not to have been updated. Apple has acknowledged the rollout problems and says it is working to resolve them. If an eligible device is no longer owned or accessible, Apple recommends removing it from the Apple Account device list.






Accessibility changes in iOS 27
Accessibility features are smarter and more intuitive in iOS 27:
VoiceOver gives richer image descriptions and better understanding of onscreen content.
Live Recognition lets users press the Action button to ask questions about their surroundings and receive detailed responses.
Voice Control is more intuitive, allowing users to describe onscreen buttons and controls rather than remembering exact coordinate labels or numbers.
Accessibility Reader is able to handle more complex source material and provide summaries and translation.






iOS 27 compatibility 

				
					

				
			iPhone 11 is supported by iOS 27.
Roman Loyola/IDG




According to Apple, iOS 27 supports iPhones back to the iPhone 11 and second-generation iPhone SE, although some Apple Intelligence and Siri AI features require newer hardware.
Support for iOS 27 does not mean every device gets every feature. Apple Intelligence and Siri AI require an iPhone 15 Pro or iPhone 16 or later, while the most advanced on-device AI models require an iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone Air, or iPhone 18 Pro. On iPad, Apple Intelligence requires an M1-class model or the A17 Pro iPad mini, while the newest on-device models require an M4 iPad with at least 12GB of RAM.
There had been speculation that the iPhone 11 series and iPhone SE 2 would miss out on iOS 27 after leaker Instant Digital claimed on Weibo that the 2019 iPhone 11, 11 Pro and 11 Pro Max, along with the 2020 iPhone SE 2, would no longer be supported. That prediction proved incorrect, giving those models at least one more year of software support.
However, the iPhone 11 generation is nearing the end of its support life. As we explain in our guide to how long Apple supports iPhones, the iPhone 11 Pro and 11 Pro Max have already been added to Apple’s Vintage iPhone list.
The iOS 27 compatibility list is:
iPhone 18 Pro
iPhone 18 Pro Max
iPhone Duo
iPhone 17e (launched in 2026) 
iPhone 17, 17 Pro / 17 Pro Max (launched in 2025)
iPhone Air (launched in 2025)
iPhone 16e (launched in 2025)
iPhone 16 / 16 Plus and iPhone 16 Pro / 16 Pro Max (launched in 2024)
iPhone 15 / 15 Plus and iPhone 15 Pro / 15 Pro Max (launched in 2023)
iPhone 14 / 14 Plus / 14 Pro / 14 Pro Max (launched in 2022)
iPhone SE 3 (launched in 2022)
iPhone 13 / 13 mini / 13 Pro / 13 Pro Max (launched in 2021)
iPhone 12 / 12 mini / 12 Pro / 12 Pro Max (launched in 2020)
iPhone SE 2 (launched in 2020)
iPhone 11 / 11 Pro / 11 Pro Max (launched in 2019)
The main dividing line for Apple Intelligence remains the iPhone 15 Pro generation: the standard iPhone 15 and all older models can run iOS 27, but they do not support Apple Intelligence.






 FAQ 


1.
When was iOS 27 released?
iOS 27 was released on September 14, 2026.





2.
Which iPhones get iOS 27?
The iPhone 11 and iPhone SE 2 and newer get iOS 27. However, Siri AI and other Apple Intelligence features require iPhone 15 Pro or newer, and the new more expressive Siri voices feature requires iPhone Air, iPhone 17 Pro, or newer.





3.
Which iPhones will get Siri AI and Apple Intelligence in iOS 27?
The only iPhones that can run Siri AI are the iPhone 15 Pro and Pro Max and any newer generation. If you have a standard iPhone 15 then you won’t get Siri AI and Apple Intelligence.

Black Friday is one of the best opportunities to save on a Mac, with retailers competing to discount MacBooks and desktop models – including recently released machines. The Black Friday Mac deals are already here, and the 13-inch M5 MacBook Air with 512GB of storage is where we’d start for most people. Amazon has listed it for $999 in the U.S. and £1,149 in the U.K., saving $300 and about £150 off Apple’s current prices. If you already have a display, keyboard, and mouse, the M6 Mac mini is a cheaper way to get a new Mac at $779 or £759.
There are bigger savings on MacBook Pro models if you need the extra power. In the U.S., Amazon has listed the 14-inch M5 Max MacBook Pro with 36GB of memory and 2TB of storage for $3,599, $500 off. In the U.K., the 16-inch M5 Pro MacBook Pro with 24GB of memory and 1TB of storage is £2,599, £400 off. That’s about £536 less than the equivalent touchscreen model on sale, so think about how much you’d benefit from the OLED display before paying the premium.
Apple’s June price increases make the advertised savings worth a closer look. The U.S. MacBook Air deal is $50 below its pre-increase price, while the U.K. offer is still about £50 above what Apple charged before June. We compare prices for the same configurations so you can see which deals are worth taking and which have been better before.
Below, we explain which Mac to buy at these prices, from the budget MacBook Neo to the Mac Studio. If you’re deciding whether to buy now or wait for Apple’s November 27–30 promotion, compare what you’d pay today with what you’d actually use from a gift card on a future purchase. For more offers, visit our Black Friday coverage and our Apple Black Friday deals roundups of the best iPad deals, Apple Watch deals and AirPods deals.

The gift card is for a future Apple purchase. Compare its value with the upfront discounts we share below. See the full Apple Black Friday offer.
Which Mac or MacBook should you buy this Black Friday?


MacBook Air – Our best overall choice 

				
					

				
			
Ida Blix




The MacBook Air is our recommendation for most buyers. Both sizes offer a lightweight, silent laptop for everyday work, studying, and occasional creative projects. Choose the 13-inch for portability or the 15-inch for more workspace without MacBook Pro pricing.
We’d prioritize a competitive price on the memory and storage you need. For regular lengthy exports or other sustained demanding tasks, consider a MacBook Pro with active cooling instead.
U.S. Black Friday price: October Prime Day brought the 13-inch M5 Air with 16GB memory and 512GB storage to $1,099, and the equivalent 15-inch to $1,299. We are already seeing up to $300 off the 13-inch models, and $300 off the 15-inch options, bringing the price below the original MSRP from before Apple increased prices. These savings are better than Apple’s $200 gift card.
U.K. Black Friday price: October offers included approximately £1,199 for the 13-inch M5 Air and £1,349 for the 15-inch, both with 512GB storage. Last Black Friday’s M4 models with 256GB reached £849 and £1,025. Match storage capacities when comparing generations. Amazon has the 13-inch M5 MacBook Air with 512GB of storage, 16GB of memory, and an 8-core GPU for £1,149, saving £150 off Apple’s £1,299 price. That’s about £50 less than it cost during October Prime Day. Amazon also has the 15-inch M5 MacBook Air with 512GB of storage and 16GB of memory for £1,299, saving £200 off Apple’s £1,499 price. Earlier in November, we saw a larger £200 discount on the 13-inch MacBook Air.
The £160 Apple gift card is close to the £150 upfront discount on the 13-inch 512GB Air.
Apple’s Deal: Apple’s £160 gift card is worth about £10 more than Amazon’s upfront discount on the 13-inch model. On the 15-inch model, Amazon’s upfront discount is £40 more than the gift card’s value.






MacBook Neo – Our budget choice, at the right price

				
					

				
			
Eugen Wegmann




The MacBook Neo suits browsing, schoolwork, streaming, and office apps. Its lower starting price makes it appealing, but its fixed 8GB of memory leaves less room for demanding workloads.
Check which configuration is discounted: only the 512GB version includes Touch ID. Both lack a backlit keyboard, MagSafe, and Thunderbolt. Compare clearance MacBook Air stock before deciding how much those compromises save you.
U.S. Black Friday price: Amazon has the 256GB MacBook Neo for $599 ($100 off) and the 512GB model with Touch ID for $699 ($100 off) – the original on-sale prices for those models before Apple increased prices in June. 
U.K. Black Friday price: The 256GB MacBook Neo is £679.97 (£19.03 off), and the 512GB model with Touch ID is £719 (£80 off).






MacBook Pro M6 – Best step up from the Air

				
					

				
			
Macbook Pro M6 Aufmacher

Halyna Kubiv




The standard M6 MacBook Pro is worth considering if you want a better built-in display, more connections, and cooling for sustained workloads without paying for a Pro or Max chip. It comes in a 14-inch size, with a non-touch Liquid Retina XDR display, HDMI, and an SDXC card slot.
It starts with 16GB memory and 1TB storage, so account for those specifications when comparing prices with an Air or older Pro. Despite the newer generation number, the standard M6 isn’t automatically the better choice for demanding work than an M5 Pro or M5 Max.
U.S. Black Friday price: The M6 model wasn’t available during October Prime Day, but it’s on offer for Black Friday with $200 off at Amazon, where it’s $1,799. B&H also has $150 off the 14-inch MacBook Pro (M6)

MacBook Pro M5 Pro – Best for demanding professional work

				
					

				
			
Foundry




The non-touchscreen M5 Pro MacBook Pro is a strong choice for development, photography, video editing, and heavier multitasking. Available in 14-inch and 16-inch sizes, it offers professional performance without the Max chip’s higher price.
Compare it with the touchscreen version using the same memory and storage. Both offer M5 Pro configurations, so a discounted non-touch model could be particularly good value if its existing XDR display meets your needs.
U.S. Black Friday price: October prices included $2,339 for the 14-inch M5 Pro with 24GB memory and 1TB storage, and $2,749 for the equivalent 16-inch. So far this Black Friday month we are seeing $300 off the 16-inch MacBook Pro with M5 Pro and $300 off the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5 Pro. MacBook Pro M5 Max – Best for demanding graphics and video

				
					

				
			
Ida Blix




Consider the non-touchscreen M5 Max MacBook Pro if your work benefits from additional graphics power or more memory than an M5 Pro supports. Complex 3D projects and demanding video production make a stronger case for it than everyday productivity.
We’d choose the configuration around the work you do. A larger advertised discount on a Max doesn’t necessarily make it better value than a less expensive Pro that meets your needs. Our MacBook Pro buying advice explains the options.

Touchscreen MacBook Pro – Best for its OLED display

				
					

				
			


Roman Loyola/Foundry




The touchscreen MacBook Pro is most compelling for its OLED display and thinner, lighter design. Improved blacks and reduced blooming could matter more to your everyday experience than touch controls, particularly if you spend most of your working day using the built-in screen.
Available in 14-inch and 16-inch sizes with M5 Pro or M5 Max chips, these models offer comparable processing performance to their non-touch equivalents. Compare matching configurations: the regular premium is $400/£400, so consider how much you’ll benefit from the display before paying extra.

Foundry




The M6 Mac mini suits buyers who already own a display, keyboard, and mouse. It offers a compact desktop for everyday work and lighter creative projects. Check storage carefully: the entry-level model has a restrictive 256GB SSD.

Ida Blix

Should you buy a Mac or MacBook now or wait for a better deal?
With Black Friday approaching, we’d avoid paying full price unless you need a Mac immediately. But sales stretch across much of November, so an early offer can be worth taking if it matches or approaches a previous low for the same configuration. Waiting can be a gamble if you’re buying clearance stock with a particular screen size, memory capacity, or finish. If the retailer discount is close to Apple’s gift card value and you already have another Apple purchase planned, it may be worth waiting until November 27 to take advantage of Apple’s gift card offer, but note that MacBook Neo, standard M6 MacBook Pro, iMac and Mac Studio are not included in Apple’s Black Friday deal. 
The M5 MacBook Air remains an appealing purchase at a good discount, with a replacement not expected until 2027. The recently updated Mac mini and Mac Studio are also worth considering if they meet your needs. The main reason to wait is a better price rather than an imminent replacement.
MacBook Pro buyers no longer need to wait for the rumored October launches: the standard M6 and OLED touchscreen models are now available. However, their recent arrival may limit initial discounts. Non-touch M5 Pro and M5 Max models could offer better value, particularly if you don’t need the touchscreen version’s improved display and lighter design. If your existing M4 or M5 MacBook Pro still meets your needs, there’s little reason to upgrade simply because a newer option exists.
The M6 iMac has only just arrived, replacing the aging M4 version. Compare a modest saving on the latest model with a substantial clearance discount on its predecessor, rather than assuming the older machine is automatically the better deal.
Previous prices need context this year. Following June’s increases, a discount from Apple’s current asking price may still leave you paying more than before the increases. Compare retailers as well: Amazon competes with Best Buy, Walmart, and B&H in the U.S., and retailers including Currys and John Lewis in the U.K. Our MacBook Pro buying advice explains the current choices.






Which Mac specifications are worth paying for?
The cheapest Mac isn’t always the best value. Use Black Friday to get a configuration that will serve you for longer within your budget, but don’t pay for performance or features you won’t use.
Check the exact chip, screen size, memory, and storage. A standard M6 and an M5 Pro or M5 Max serve different needs: the newer generation number alone doesn’t tell you which is better for your work. For MacBook Pro listings, distinguish the OLED touchscreen version from non-touch models.
Avoid saving a small amount by buying too little memory or storage. Most current Macs start with 16GB of unified memory, but the MacBook Neo has a fixed 8GB, and some desktop configurations include only a 256GB SSD. Unified memory cannot be upgraded later. An external SSD can add storage, but it cannot compensate for insufficient RAM.
Once the processor meets your needs, additional memory may be more useful than a faster chip. Compare a discounted Air with the Neo, too: the M5 Air starts with twice the memory and storage of the entry-level Neo. Our Mac buying guide explains which specifications suit different workloads.
Check whether the configuration includes nano-texture glass. This optional finish reduces glare and reflections, which can help in bright rooms or near windows, but increases the price. If reflections rarely bother you, standard glass may offer better value.






Should you buy an older Mac or MacBook?

				
					

				
			
Foundry




An older Mac can be excellent value if its price reflects its age and configuration. Compare its actual selling price with the discounted price of the newer equivalent, rather than focusing on a large percentage saving from its original launch price.
Previous-generation Apple silicon models are the most promising starting point. A discounted M4 MacBook Air or standard M5 MacBook Pro may meet your needs comfortably. Older Pro and Max configurations can also be worth considering if they provide the memory, graphics performance, and connections your work requires for substantially less money.
Check what the saving buys—and what you give up. An older Mac with more memory or storage could be more useful than a newer entry-level configuration. Conversely, a cheaper older Air with 256GB storage isn’t directly comparable with an M5 Air that starts with 512GB. The non-touch M5 Pro and M5 Max MacBook Pros also remain current options, despite the arrival of the standard M6 and touchscreen models.
Be much more cautious with Intel Macs. Their software support is winding down, and a low purchase price may leave you with a machine that has a limited useful life for current apps and macOS features. Check compatibility with the software you need before buying any older model.
For used or refurbished Macs, check battery condition on laptops, warranty coverage, and the returns policy. Confirm that Activation Lock has been removed and that the Mac isn’t still enrolled in an organization’s management system.
For more advice read:
Should I buy a MacBook Neo?
Should I buy a MacBook Air?
Should I buy a MacBook Pro?
Should I buy a Mac mini?
Should I buy a Mac Studio?






Mac or MacBook deals to avoid
Treat large advertised discounts carefully. Following June’s price increases, “$400 off” may simply bring a Mac closer to what it cost before the increase. Compare previous selling prices for the same configuration, rather than judging the offer solely against today’s recommended price.
Check whether the price includes AppleCare+ or another protection plan. Some Amazon listings bundle coverage with the Mac. If you don’t want it, a listing without coverage could be cheaper; if you do, compare the bundle with buying the Mac and coverage separately.
Check for a bundled power adapter, too. Some Mac laptops are sold without one in the U.K. and EU. A charger bundle may be useful if you need an adapter, but could mean paying extra unnecessarily if you already own a suitable one.
Compare the complete setup cost. A Mac mini or Studio requires a display, keyboard, and mouse or trackpad, while adapters and docks can add to the cost of any Mac.
Finally, distinguish cash discounts from gift cards, trade-ins, financing, and membership-only offers. Read the conditions, check the seller, and confirm whether the Mac is new, refurbished, or used, along with its warranty and returns policy.






How we choose Mac and MacBook deals
Macworld has covered the Mac since its launch in 1984, and our recommendations draw on decades of experience and hands-on reviews. We consider performance, display quality, battery life, portability, connectivity, and everyday use alongside price to explain which Macs suit different buyers.
Our reviews help us assess which upgrades are worth paying for. We look at whether additional processing power benefits demanding workloads, when more memory is useful, and whether a premium display justifies the extra cost. A MacBook Air may offer better value for everyday work, while a Pro, Max, or Ultra configuration needs to earn its higher price through the work it enables.
We combine those findings with current prices and previous offers, matching the exact chip, screen size, memory, and storage. Following Apple’s June price increases, we also consider earlier selling prices rather than judging a deal solely against today’s recommended retail price. A large advertised discount doesn’t automatically make an offer exceptional.
We consider the complete purchase, too: the retailer, product condition, warranty, and any conditions attached to the price. For desktop Macs, we also account for the display and accessories you’ll need. Our Mac buying guide and MacBook comparison explain how to choose the right model and configuration.

Stay tuned to Macworld between Black Friday and Cyber Monday to find the best deals as they arrive. But if you’re looking for a specific color or capacity, you can check out the following retailers. In the U.S., here are the best stores to shop for Black Friday deals:
Apple – no direct discounts, gift card giveaway confirmed
Amazon – widest range and often the deepest short-term discounts, but stock moves quickly
Adorama – a wide range of Macs that includes older models.

How we pick the best Apple deals
At Macworld we’ve been covering and reviewing Apple and Apple devices for more than 40 years, from the original Macintosh to the most recent M6 MacBook Pro and iPhone 18 Pro. Our recommendations draw on hands-on reviews and price comparisons, and we use Apple products every day (and buy most of them ourselves), so we know a good deal when we see one.
With a working knowledge of everything Apple sells and decades of experience, we know when stores are inflating MSRPs or pushing “normal” sales as limited Black Friday deals. Rest assured, the listings you see here will only be for the best discounts we can find on that particular item.

title: Best AirPods 2026: Which AirPods should you buy?
content:
Macworld





Apple’s AirPods lineup falls into three main families: AirPods 5, AirPods Pro 3, and AirPods Max 2. For most buyers, the choice is between AirPods 5 and AirPods Pro 3. AirPods 5 start at $129 and combine an open-ear design with Active Noise Cancellation, while the $249 AirPods Pro 3 use foam-infused silicone tips for a more secure fit and stronger noise isolation. They also add heart-rate sensing and Apple’s hearing-health features. AirPods Max 2 are a different proposition: $549 over-ear headphones for buyers who value sound quality and noise cancellation and prefer an over-ear fit. Right now is a fantastic time to buy AirPods because, thanks to Black Friday prices, there are some excellent bargains to be had. 
Best Black Friday AirPods deals: U.S.
AirPods Pro 3: $149 ($100 off at Amazon, MSRP $249)
AirPods Max 2: $419 ($130 off at Amazon, MSRP $549)
Best Black Friday AirPods deals: U.K.
AirPods Pro 3: £155.98 (£63 off at Amazon, RRP £219).
AirPods 5 (wireless charging case): £119 (£20 off at Amazon, RRP £139).
PRICES CHECKED NOVEMBER 26, 2026 – Deals change quickly, so we will update this page throughout November
When deciding which AirPods to buy, start with the fit you’ll be happy wearing for hours, then compare what you’d actually pay for the features you’ll use. If you prefer an open fit, AirPods 5 are the better buy, and the wireless charging version is worth a small premium for its longer battery life and swipe volume controls. If a sale brings AirPods Pro 3 close to the price of AirPods 5 and you’re comfortable with silicone tips, the Pro 3 are the better value for their stronger noise cancellation and longer battery life. Even at a discount, AirPods Max 2 make the most sense if you specifically want over-ear headphones.
In this guide, we compare Apple’s current AirPods on fit, sound, noise cancellation, battery life, hearing features, and price. We also explain which version of AirPods 5 to buy and when a discount makes an older model worth considering.


Which AirPods are the best?
We recommend AirPods Pro 3 as the best AirPods overall, thanks to their combination of noise cancellation, secure fit, longer battery life and additional health features.
For many people, however, AirPods 5 will be the better buy. They now include Active Noise Cancellation, Adaptive Audio, Transparency mode and Conversation Awareness, closing much of the feature gap with the Pro model while costing substantially less. They’re also the obvious choice if you prefer an open fit rather than silicone ear tips.
AirPods Max 2 are best considered separately. They are over-ear headphones rather than earbuds and cost more than twice as much as AirPods Pro 3, so they make most sense for buyers specifically looking for that style of headphone.

Best for: Buyers who want the strongest combination of ANC, fit, battery life and features.
Buy AirPods Pro 3 if: You want the best noise cancellation of Apple’s earbuds, longer battery life, a secure in-ear fit or the health and hearing features.
Don’t buy AirPods Pro 3 if: You dislike earbuds that seal the ear canal or don’t need enough of their extra features to justify spending $100–$120 more than on AirPods 5.
For most buyers who don’t object to silicone ear tips, AirPods Pro 3 are the best AirPods you can buy.
Released in September 2025, the third-generation AirPods Pro improved on an already excellent pair of earbuds without increasing the $249 launch price. In our review, Jason Cross praised their more comfortable and secure fit, improved battery life, better noise cancellation and Transparency mode, and effective heart-rate sensor. Taken together, those apparently small changes add up to a significant improvement.
The biggest physical change is the fit. AirPods Pro 3 have redesigned earbuds with foam-infused tips available in five sizes, including XXS. In our testing, they stayed securely in place even during intense activity and felt more comfortable than the previous generation.
Noise cancellation is another major advantage. Apple says AirPods Pro 3 remove twice as much noise as AirPods Pro 2, while our review also found improvements to noise reduction, Transparency mode and bass response.
Battery life is strong too. Apple rates the earbuds for up to eight hours with ANC enabled, an estimate that was broadly borne out in our testing. The charging case takes total ANC listening time to up to 24 hours.
AirPods Pro 3 also have features the AirPods 5 don’t. The built-in heart-rate sensor works with workouts in the Fitness app, while Apple’s Hearing Test, Hearing Aid and Hearing Protection features make the Pro model particularly compelling for users interested in hearing health.

Don’t buy AirPods 5 if: Maximum isolation and noise cancellation are important, or you want heart-rate sensing and Apple’s hearing-health features.
AirPods 5 are no longer simply the cheaper AirPods that miss out on most of the Pro features.
Apple introduced AirPods 5 in September 2026 with Active Noise Cancellation as standard. That immediately makes the decision more interesting: you can now get open-ear AirPods with ANC for $129, compared with $249 for AirPods Pro 3.
Like previous standard AirPods, they don’t use silicone ear tips. They sit in the ear without sealing the ear canal, which will be an important advantage for anyone who finds AirPods Pro uncomfortable or dislikes the isolated feeling of in-ear earbuds.
Noise cancellation is much improved. Apple says AirPods 5 remove up to 50 percent more external noise than AirPods 4 with ANC, thanks to a redesigned acoustic architecture and updated computational audio. Macworld also notes that Transparency mode has been improved and that Adaptive Audio can automatically blend ANC and Transparency according to your surroundings.
Sound has been upgraded too, with a new acoustic design and next-generation Adaptive EQ intended to improve performance across a wider range of ear shapes.
There are actually two AirPods 5 packages, but unlike the previous generation they don’t differ in whether ANC is included.
The $129 AirPods 5 come with a USB-C charging case. Apple rates these for up to four hours of listening with ANC enabled or six hours with noise control turned off, and up to 20 hours with the case when using ANC.
The $149 AirPods 5 with Wireless Charging Case are the more compelling option. They can charge over USB-C, with an Apple Watch charger or with a Qi charger, and the case includes a speaker for Find My. They also add volume adjustment by swiping the stem. Battery life rises to as much as five hours with ANC, seven hours with noise control off and 22 hours with the case when using ANC.
At only $20 more, we’d lean toward the Wireless Charging Case version unless you’re particularly keen to keep the price down.

Apple introduced AirPods Max 2 in March 2026, finally replacing the original AirPods Max with a model powered by the H2 chip. The change brought features including Adaptive Audio, Conversation Awareness, Voice Isolation and Live Translation to the AirPods Max line.
Sound quality remains excellent. Our review also rated the Active Noise Cancellation and Transparency mode among the model’s strongest attributes. Apple says ANC is up to 1.5 times more effective than on the previous generation.

AirPods 5 vs AirPods Pro 3: Which should you buy?

				
					

				
			
AirPods Pro 3 vs AirPods 5

Foundry





AirPods 5 are better if…
You dislike earbuds that seal your ear canal.
You want to spend less.
An open fit is more important than maximum noise isolation.
You want ANC but don’t need the Pro health features.
AirPods Pro 3 are better if…
You want Apple’s hearing-health features.
Strong noise cancellation is a priority.
You want longer battery life.
You want a more secure in-ear fit.
You want heart-rate sensing.
The difference between standard AirPods and AirPods Pro used to be straightforward: standard AirPods were cheaper and open-fitting, while the Pros added ANC and Apple’s more sophisticated listening modes.
With the AirPods 5, that distinction is less clear. Both AirPods 5 and AirPods Pro 3 use Apple’s H2 chip and support Active Noise Cancellation, Adaptive Audio, Transparency mode, Conversation Awareness, Voice Isolation and Personalized Spatial Audio.
The remaining differences are nevertheless significant.
Design and fit
AirPods 5 use an open-ear design and don’t use ear tips. AirPods Pro 3 sit more tightly in the ear canal and come with foam-infused silicone tips in five sizes. When we reviewed the AirPods Pro 3 we found the redesigned tips substantially improved comfort and security and kept the earbuds in place during strenuous exercise.
Choose AirPods 5 if you don’t like the plugged-ear sensation of silicone tips.
Choose AirPods Pro 3 if you want a tighter, more secure fit and better isolation.
Noise cancellation
AirPods 5 include Active Noise Cancellation as standard, unlike AirPods 4, which were sold with or without ANC. But their open-ear design means they approach noise reduction differently from the AirPods Pro 3.
AirPods Pro 3 use ear tips to create a seal in the ear canal, giving them a natural advantage when it comes to isolation. Apple says their ANC removes up to twice as much noise as AirPods Pro 2, and in our testing both noise cancellation and Transparency mode were improved over the previous generation.
AirPods 5 don’t create a seal, but their open-ear ANC is significantly more effective than before. Apple says they remove up to 50 percent more external noise than AirPods 4 with ANC.
AirPods 5 are the better choice if you dislike the feeling of a sealed in-ear fit.
AirPods Pro 3 remain the better choice if maximum noise reduction and isolation are your priorities.
Battery life
AirPods Pro 3 have a significant battery advantage. They last up to eight hours with ANC enabled and up to 24 hours including the charging case.
The $129 AirPods 5 manage up to four hours with ANC, while the $149 Wireless Charging Case version increases that to five hours.
That’s a substantial difference if you frequently use your AirPods for long journeys or extended listening sessions.

Health and hearing features
The AirPods Pro 3 include a heart-rate sensor that can measure your heart rate during workouts, and our reviewer found the results comparable to an Apple Watch during testing.
They also support Apple’s Hearing Test, Hearing Aid and Hearing Protection features.
Those features aren’t available on AirPods 5.
AirPods Pro 3 are also the obvious choice if Apple’s health features are important.
Price
The Pro model costs $100 more than the AirPods 5 with Wireless Charging Case and $120 more than the cheapest version.
The gap can shrink during sales. AirPods Pro 3 fell to $149 during Black Friday 2026, which is the same price as the AirPods 5 with wireless charging, so it’s always worth checking the live price comparison before deciding.
AirPods 5 start at $129, or $149 with the Wireless Charging Case.
AirPods Pro 3 are $249.






Which AirPods 5 should you get? 
Unlike AirPods 4, Apple doesn’t sell one AirPods 5 model with ANC and another without it. All AirPods 5 have Active Noise Cancellation.
Instead, the choice is between cases.
The $129 model has a USB-C charging case. It offers up to four hours of battery life with ANC and up to 20 hours including the case.
For $149, the Wireless Charging Case can also charge using an Apple Watch charger or Qi charger and includes a speaker for Find My. The earbuds in this package also support volume adjustment by swiping the stems. Battery life increases to five hours with ANC and 22 hours with the case.
Our recommendation: Buy the version with wireless charging case – given the relatively small $20 difference, the $149 version is the better buy for most people.






Should you buy older AirPods?
We’d generally recommend buying the latest generation rather than deliberately seeking out older AirPods because there is a considerable gap between the different generations. 
Should you buy AirPods 4?
AirPods 5 start at the same $129 MSRP previously charged for AirPods 4 without ANC, but now include ANC as standard, along with improved noise cancellation and sound quality.
That makes AirPods 4 difficult to recommend unless you find them at a substantial clearance discount. They dropped to $99 during Prime Day 2026, but with AirPods 5 now available at $129, we’d want to see them priced noticeably lower than that.
Our recommendation: Only buy AirPods 4 at a steep discount.

Should you buy AirPods Pro 2?
AirPods Pro 2 remain capable earbuds, but AirPods Pro 3 improve the fit, noise cancellation and battery life, while adding heart-rate sensing.
Our recommendation: We’d buy AirPods Pro 2 only if they’re at least $30 or £30 cheaper than the best AirPods Pro 3 price you can get. If the gap is smaller, we’d pay the difference for the Pro 3’s stronger noise cancellation, longer battery life, and improved fit.
Should you buy the original AirPods Max?
AirPods Max 2 retain many aspects of the original design but add the H2 chip, which enables Adaptive Audio, Conversation Awareness, Voice Isolation and Live Translation. ANC has also been improved.
If you’re going to spend close to AirPods Max money, the second-generation model is therefore the one to get.

 FAQ 


1.
What’s the difference between AirPods and AirPods Pro?
The biggest difference is fit. AirPods 5 use an open-ear design, while AirPods Pro 3 use foam-infused silicone tips that seal the ear canal.
Both now have Active Noise Cancellation, Adaptive Audio, Transparency mode and Conversation Awareness. AirPods Pro 3 nevertheless offer stronger isolation, longer ANC battery life and exclusive features including heart-rate sensing, Hearing Test, Hearing Aid and Hearing Protection.
AirPods 5 start at $129; AirPods Pro 3 cost $249.





2.
Do AirPods work with Macs and iPads?
Yes. AirPods work particularly well with Apple devices.
Once your AirPods are paired, they can automatically connect to devices associated with your Apple account, and Automatic Device Switching can move playback between devices depending on what you’re using.
Apple lists current versions of macOS and iPadOS among the supported platforms for AirPods 5, AirPods Pro 3 and AirPods Max 2.





3.
Can you use AirPods with non-Apple devices?
Yes. AirPods are Bluetooth headphones and can be used with non-Apple hardware.
We have, for example, demonstrated how AirPods can be paired directly with a Nintendo Switch using its Bluetooth Audio settings.
Apple also explicitly states that current AirPods can be used as Bluetooth headphones with non-Apple devices, although some functionality may be limited.
The main reason to use AirPods with Apple hardware is therefore the deeper ecosystem integration rather than basic Bluetooth compatibility.





4.
Do AirPods have Find My?
Yes, but the capabilities depend on the model and case.
AirPods can be located through Apple’s Find My system. The $149 AirPods 5 Wireless Charging Case includes a speaker for Find My alerts, while the standard $129 USB-C case does not. AirPods Pro 3 also include a speaker in their MagSafe charging case.
Find My support is useful not just for locating misplaced AirPods but also when checking whether a suspicious pair of AirPods behaves as genuine Apple hardware. See our guide to spotting fake AirPods for more advice.





5.
Are AirPods waterproof?
No. AirPods aren’t “waterproof”, but they do offer some water resistance. 
AirPods 5 are rated IP57 for dust, sweat and water resistance. AirPods Pro 3 and their charging case are also rated IP57.
That makes them suitable for exercise and provides protection against water exposure, but water resistance isn’t the same thing as waterproofing and shouldn’t be taken as an invitation to use them for swimming.
AirPods Max 2 don’t have a water-resistance rating.

title: Turn your iPhone Duo into the world’s smallest laptop with this cute app
content:
Macworld





Every time I refer to the iPhone Duo as “Apple’s first foldable product” I pause for a moment and wonder: do laptops count? After all, they’ve had a folding hinge for decades. The iPhone Duo, if you think about it, is really just a tiny laptop.
If that strikes you as a whimsical thought, you’ll be delighted to hear about a newly updated app which offers to make that comparison a reality. A really, really cute reality.
Screens 5: VNC Remote Desktop is, as the name suggests, an app which enables you to remotely share screens between devices. You can use it, for example, to access your work MacBook on your iPhone, iPad, another Mac, or Vision Pro. It’s a largely work-focused app that you’d expect to focus on productivity rather than eye-catching features.
But with the version 5.10.6 update, which was rolled out for the iPhone on November 25 (maker Edovia says the equivalent update for the Mac version is awaiting App Store approval), something rather fun has been added: Laptop Mode for iPhone Duo. When you use this mode on a semi-folded Duo and connect to a MacBook, the shared output is displayed in a way which mimics the layout of a laptop. “Simply fold your iPhone Duo halfway to turn it into a pocket-sized workstation, with your remote desktop on the upper half and a custom keyboard and trackpad below,” Edovia explains in a blog post.
It’s absolutely adorable. And functional, too. “The trackpad supports the same familiar gestures you’ve come to expect from Screens,” Edovia adds, “while the custom keyboard supports multiple languages, follows your selected system keyboard language, and lets you swipe down on keys to access secondary characters, just like on iPad.”
Screens is officially a free app, but it has pretty much zero functionality without a subscription. If you’re keen to try out the new mode and turn your iPhone Duo into a tiny laptop, you could start a trial subscription, but (assuming you don’t find the app so useful that you decide to use it in the long term) remember to cancel it before you get charged. It’s a cute feature, but on its own it probably isn’t worth $4.99 a month.

The SlideTag's design draws on Kodak's Kodachrome slide mounts, placing a square display inside a retro frame with an attachment point for a keyring. Users can manage photos through the Kodak Memory Link app for iOS and Android, separately from the accessory's tracking features. Find My app, the SlideTag can be located through the ‌Find My‌ network. There is also support for Google's Find Hub. A built-in buzzer provides an audible way to find nearby belongings.
